content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm having trouble connecting to my [product_name] using [product_name] software. Whenever I attempt to download the program, it requests a password. I've tried various options like 'logo', 'admin', 'LOGO', and 'ADMIN', but none work and I keep receiving an HTTP authentication failed error stating the password may be incorrect. Despite all my attempts, I can't get past this error. Thanks for any advice!

Hello, Try these steps: Disable all Ethernet connections on your computer except for the one linked to [product_name]. Connect [product_name] directly via Ethernet cable (no other devices). Retrieve IP information from the [product_name] display. Ensure you're selecting the correct [product_name] version in the software. If this doesn't help: Use the PC with [product_name] Software, go to tools/transfer, and select 'delete user program and password.' Hope this helps!

Hi [user_name], I've tried all your suggestions but still can't resolve the issue. I can connect to the PLC, but it keeps asking for a password every time. The PLC is brand new, but nothing I'm doing works. Thanks!

Hello, Please share the firmware version installed on your [product_name] (diagnostics/software/FW-version) and the [product_name] software version on your computer (Help/About). Also, which [product_name] version did you choose in the software?

Hello, I'm experiencing the same issue as the member mentioned earlier, regarding a [product_name]. I've also tried all the expert advice, including changing the mode from standard to FS4. The code for the [product_name] is [article_no] and firmware is [version_no]. After resetting to factory settings and switching between OP and Admin with the code 'LOGO', it works.

I have the same issue with my new [product_name]. Even after a factory reset, I keep getting the HTTP authentication error with firmware [version_no]. What should I do? Update: Upgrading the [product_name] software to v8.2 helped solve the issue!
One known issue is if the connection doesn't establish quickly enough after initiating, a password prompt may appear—even if no password was set for that action.
Hello, Which [product_name] version did you use when configuring your project?
Were you able to resolve this problem?

Upgrading to the latest [product_name] software (8.2 SP1) seems to fix the issue, as mentioned earlier. The problem occurred with older software versions and was also related to slow LAN communication. Regards, [user_name]

I often see this password prompt when connecting to a [product_name] on a subnet different from the one my Comfort software is running on. For example: 1. Launching Comfort software on 192.168.1.xxx, then switching network to 192.168.2.xxx while [product_name] is on 192.168.2.xxx. 2. [product_name] is connected to a separate subnet. 3. Accessing [product_name] via dynamic DNS, not on the same network. It appears the Comfort software switches to port 8080 for communication in these cases, making it repeatedly request the password for every action. Software improvements could include accepting the password once per session and remembering it, rather than asking after every operation.

I only see this error message when the [product_name] software tries to connect, and the device responds with a delay. If it takes too long, it fails to connect. If the device is on a different subnet and there's no gateway, I get another error. Maybe '[product_name] Support' should respond to this—I've flagged the issue as support-relevant.

All relevant tips seem to have been mentioned, so I'm inclined to think there's a problem with the PC's Ethernet port. Here's a summary of how to optimize your setup: Ensure you have administrative rights on your PC (e.g., Windows Administrator). Connect PC and [product_name] directly via Ethernet cable. Avoid running other applications that could access the Ethernet port. Make sure both PC and [product_name] are on the same subnet and use the same subnet mask. Only use valid IP/subnet mask combinations (e.g., mask 255.255.255.0 and IP ending *.255 are not valid). Don't configure a gateway. For firmware [version_no], select [product_name] FS4. Use at least [product_name] software V8.2.0.

Hello, A customer had the same issue and couldn't find a solution in this thread. He realized the problem was with selecting the correct Ethernet interface. If you're still having trouble, ensure you're using the right network interface. Good luck!

Hi, I encountered the same problem with [product_name] software 8.2 and [product_name] FS4, but found a workaround: If I open [product_name] software first, then my program, and transfer, it always prompts for a password and transfers slowly. However, if I double-click my program to launch [product_name] software, the transfer proceeds quickly and without a password request. This method works consistently, though it's a bit odd. Good luck! [user_name]

Hi everyone, I faced the same problem transferring from PC to [product_name]: slow connection and unexpected password requests even when none were set. I'm using SC 8.2.1. The solution, as mentioned earlier, was to close SoftComfort, disable my Wi-Fi adapter in Windows (leaving only Ethernet enabled), restart SoftComfort, and then everything worked smoothly—with fast transfers and no password prompts.
You might have tried accessing [product_name] via a Wi-Fi adapter. In [product_name] software, you can select which driver will be used to connect to the device.

For me, the password prompt only appeared for the first few downloads or uploads. After that, it stopped. Sometimes, when downloading programs to [product_name], I get warnings about I/O numbers not matching the hardware configuration. Although unclear, I manage to download successfully, but the hardware doesn't function as expected. I then try deleting the program or doing a factory reset to fix it.
I tried, but it's still not working.
Welcome to the forum, [user_name]. What exactly did you try?
Hello, To resolve this issue and use any connection, upgrade the software to version 8.2 SP1.

Hello all, I encountered this problem after updating the software to version 8.3 and using a new BM 8.2 FS:04. Based on previous suggestions, entering 'LOGO' (all capitals) worked and the software accepted it. After a factory reset, the password prompt disappeared. Thanks, [user_name]!

If you can't switch to Admin, go to: Tools > Transfer > Clear User Program and Password > Access Control > Online Settings > Control operation from [product_name] TD. Here, you can set a new password and then access your card to upload your program without needing your laptop. Hope this helps.
Excellent, proceed with firmware update.

When connecting to [product_name], I usually encounter a password prompt if the device is on a different subnet than the one I am on while running the Comfort software. For instance: a) Opening Comfort on subnet 192.168.1.xxx, then switching to 192.168.2.xxx while [product_name] is on 192.168.2.xxx; c) Connecting to [product_name] through dynamic DNS, not on the same network. Apparently, Comfort detects the device on a separate subnet and uses port 8080, which triggers repeated password requests. Allowing users to enter the password once per session and having the software remember it would be helpful.

analysis.insight_summary: Many users face unexpected password prompts when connecting to new [product_name] devices via [product_name] software, even after factory resets and trying typical passwords. These authentication issues occur across different firmware versions and often relate to compatibility with software versions or slow network connections. Upgrading the [product_name] software frequently resolves the problem, indicating compatibility and software versions play a major role in the connection process.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to connect seamlessly to new [product_name] devices using routine steps and default passwords, or none if not previously configured, and want direct, clear feedback if further action is needed.
